text:
samir: heads up, apiserver p50/p95 jumpy in eu-west1 since ~08:10 UTC, controller-manager leader flips a few times, and a handful of apiserver pods report OOMKilled/FD spikes. Anyone on this?

maria: seeing the same on dashboards. apiserver CPU goes to ~85% concurrent with a surge in outbound connections. Cloud NAT ephemeral ports trending to exhaustion. :eyes:

leo: checked host metrics, nvme iops look fine but kernel shows lots of sockets in TIME_WAIT. netstat on a controlplane box: `wc -l <(ss -tan state time-wait)` ~ 42k.

aj: that level of TIME_WAIT will cause fd pressure. Could be our model-worker autoscaler fanout trying to attach GPUs in parallel to many nodes. Those attach flows generate many short TCP connections to the controlplane.

samir: logs from apiserver show repeated `accept` backlog warnings and `too many open files` spikes on the proxy. Controller-manager logs show leader election timeout: `failed to renew lease` then immediate restart.

kate: I pushed a quick grafana panel for conntrack and nat usage to the incident dash. NAT port pools at ~96% for eu-west1-nat-1.

oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-562 - apiserver conn churn / leader-election-flap (assigned: eng-sre)

maria: short-term mitigation: throttled autoscaler parallel attach from 100 -> 8 for the affected batch via canary config on the autoscale-controller. That should reduce the fanout in ~60s. :white_check_mark:

leo: also temporarily added two additional external NAT IPs for eu-west1 to increase ephemeral port space. Hoping to avoid immediate reconnect storms while we triage.

aj: nice. For next steps we should: 1) enforce client-side connection reuse in the attach workflow, 2) tune tcp_tw_reuse/tcp_fin_timeout maybe, 3) increase apiserver ulimit and fd soft limits, 4) add per-cluster egress scaling controls.

samir: can someone run `kubectl -n kube-system logs apiserver-0 --tail=200` and paste the accept/errno lines? Also netstat checks on at least 2 controlplane nodes to confirm TIME_WAIT counts.

maria: pasted snippet:
```
E0320 08:12:11.123456 1 server.go:123] failed to accept connection: accept tcp 0.0.0.0:6443: too many open files
E0320 08:12:11.234567 1 wrap.go:45] error writing response: write tcp 10.0.1.2:6443->10.12.8.5:52344: write: connection reset by peer
```

leo: run `ss -s` on cp-01: TIME-WAIT: 41890, closed: 512, orphaned: 0. Kernel tcp_fin_timeout currently 60s.

aj: sounds like the root cause is heavy short-lived connections from the attach flow plus NAT port exhaustion resulting in connection failures -> leader election jitter. Two-pronged fix: application-level (reuse/pooling) + infra-level (ephemeral capacity, conntrack tuning).

kate: I opened a follow-up ticket to add a backoff into the attach controller when NAT utilization > 80%. Also flagged this as a rollout-safe change (canary first). Ticket: INFRA-2178.

samir: downscoped immediate ops: keep autoscaler throttled while we validate, monitor leader-election count metric, and watch apiserver FD usage. If p50 doesn't settle in 10m, we'll revert autoscaler to fully paused and failover to backup region for critical workloads.

maria: p50 already dropping after throttling. leader-election events dropped from 8/min -> 0-1/min. NAT usage down to 72%.

leo: follow-ups for next week: evaluate using longer-lived gRPC attach channel for GPU attach API to cut connection churn, add per-node connection pooling in autoscaler, and baseline ulimit/conntrack across controlplane images.

aj: also recommend a small permanent egress pool expansion for eu-west1 (2 extra NAT IPs) and alerting on NAT ephemeral > 80% + leader-election rate > 1/min.

samir: great. I'll write up post-incident note after stable. Thanks for the quick triage team. :thumbsup:
